newsitem.title: ITALY: UPS Italia managers, unions meet on layoffs.
newsitem.headline: UPS Italia managers, unions meet on layoffs.

text.p: Unions representing workers at United Parcel Services(UPS) Italia met the company's local management on Friday to discuss the latter's plan to layoff 150 out of 900 workers, union and company sources said.
The plan was announced on March 6 and could begin to take effect 45 days from then.

Union sources said that at the meeting they rejected the cutback saying it was unjustified on economic grounds. They added that they believe the plan may be related to possible moves to alter UPS shift working patterns in Italy.
They also invoked a procedure under the country's national transport industrial relations rules which will require both sides to discuss the proposed layoffs in a joint committee, the sources said.

A reply from UPS Italia was expected within the next fortnight, they added. In a separate statement, UPS management said meetings have taken place with union representatives in both Milan and Rome and will take place between now and April 20 "in each of the other offices involved in the reorganisation process started by UPS Italia".
It added it will examine any proposals put forward at a local level ahead of a national meeting with the unions in the near future.
